That promise didn't die with her. Researchers are now finding that inherited trauma actually sits in the DNA itself — the same way a dog bred for aggression passes down the trait, the body passes down the fear. You didn't choose it, and you've probably never even felt it as a decision. It just runs, quietly, every time you get close to someone.

It isn't bad luck. Whatever you're broadcasting, consciously or not, is the frequency the universe matches back to you — the same way a radio dialed to 94.5 will never pick up classical music no matter how many times you spin the knob wishing it would. You can scream at the dial. It won't change the station. Only changing the frequency changes what shows up.

Truth and honesty aren't the same thing, and the gap between them is where distance builds, one small omission at a time, until you're sleeping next to a stranger and can't explain why.

What's actually true is simpler and kinder: there are many people you could build that life with. The pressure of finding "the one" is optional, and it's been working against you.

"You complete me" sounds romantic. It's actually a warning sign.

If you need someone else to feel whole, you're not in a relationship, you're in a dependency wearing a relationship's clothes. Two whole people come together and create a third thing, an "us," without either person disappearing into the other. The moment you're only half without them is the moment the relationship starts running on fear instead of love.
